title: Bronson buys Lester a cheap Pan-American tenor
summary: Bronson had one sax, so Lester asked for a tenor and Bronson bought a poor Pan-American; Lester owned Buescher alto and soprano.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You were saying that when he joined Bronson, he just started playing tenor. Is that it?

Yeah. Because see, Bronson was organizing the band. Bronson had one saxophone, and a trumpet, and piano, and a bass -- a guy who was playing tuba. That's what he had; that was Bronson's band. And we came there, then he had three more. The other guy, Boswell, was playing alto. So Les said, 'Well, get me a tenor.' So Bronson went down to the store and got him a Pan-American tenor -- I'll never forget it!
Yeah! You don't remember that one, do you?
No. You know, a cheap horn. Les had a Buesher's. He had a Buesher alto and Buesher soprano.
